youtube.baslik: If the same tone reaches both ears, where is it heard? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The Stenger test rests on a simple perceptual principle: when the same tone is presented to both ears at once, a person hears it only in the ear where it seems louder. If someone claiming a one-sided loss stops responding, the result is called a positive Stenger and indicates a nonorganic component. The result is always interpreted with other tests.

instagram.kanca: If the same tone reaches both ears, where is it heard?
bilgiler: With the same tone in both ears, it is heard only in the louder ear.
Better ear: 10 dB above threshold; poorer ear: 10 dB below the claim.
If responses stop, a positive Stenger indicates a nonorganic component.

cumleler: Same tone in both ears: it is heard only where louder.
The better ear gets a tone about ten decibels above threshold.
The poorer ear gets it ten decibels below the claimed threshold.
If responses stop, a positive Stenger indicates a nonorganic component.
The result is always read with other tests, without blame.
